headline: Hospice growth and lighter Medicare Cap hit lift earnings
summary_short: Revenue rose 8.8% y/y to $673M as VITAS hospice revenue grew 11.9% and Roto-Rooter grew 3.3%; diluted EPS jumped 43.7% y/y to $5.13, helped by a much smaller Medicare Cap billing limitation than a year ago.
summary_long: Consolidated revenue rose 8.8% y/y to $673.3M as VITAS hospice revenue grew 11.9% on a 6.1% increase in days-of-care, a 2.4% Medicare rate increase, and a $15.9M smaller Medicare Cap billing limitation than Q2 2025; Roto-Rooter grew 3.3% on higher plumbing, drain-cleaning and excavation pricing, partly offset by weaker water restoration. Gross margin expanded to 32.9% from 29.8%, largely on the smaller Medicare Cap headwind at VITAS. SG&A rose 10.9% on higher Roto-Rooter advertising and VITAS legal costs. Diluted EPS was $5.13, up 43.7% y/y. Cash rose q/q to $40.2M even as the company drew $140M in new long-term debt and repurchased $287.5M of stock over six months; no formal forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: VITAS revenue rose 11.9% on a 6.1% days-of-care increase, a 2.4% Medicare rate increase, and a $15.9M smaller Medicare Cap billing limitation than Q2 2025; Roto-Rooter grew 3.3% on higher plumbing, drain-cleaning and excavation pricing, partly offset by weaker water restoration.
Cost of revenue grew only 4.1% while revenue grew 8.8%, consistent with the release's description of a smaller Medicare Cap billing limitation and pricing gains at Roto-Rooter outpacing cost growth.

Operating income growth of 31.0% outpaced revenue growth as consolidated gross margin expanded to 32.9% from 29.8%, mainly on VITAS's smaller Medicare Cap billing limitation ($0.5M this quarter vs $16.4M a year ago).
Pretax income growth (28.4%) lagged operating income growth (31.0%) due to a $1.3M y/y increase in interest expense tied to higher long-term debt used for acquisitions and stock repurchases.
Net income growth of 29.0% closely tracked pretax income growth; the effective tax rate was little changed at 25.9% versus 26.2% a year ago.
EPS growth (42.8%) exceeded net income growth (29.0%) because weighted-average basic shares fell about 9.7% y/y as the company repurchased $287.5M of stock over six months.
Same dynamic as basic EPS: 29.0% net income growth combined with a 10.2% y/y decline in diluted share count (13.2M vs 14.7M) from ongoing buybacks drives the 43.7% EPS increase.
Cash rose q/q as $173.0M of six-month operating cash flow and $140M drawn on the new revolving credit facility funded $287.5M of buybacks and $33.5M of acquisitions.
The $140.0 million increase in long-term debt is due primarily to acquisitions and stock repurchases, per the company's own liquidity disclosure.
Equity fell 2.1% q/q as $287.5M of six-month treasury stock repurchases outweighed six months of net income, also driving a $291.9 million increase in treasury stock.
Diluted share count fell 10.2% y/y to 13.2 million as the company repurchased $287.5 million of stock in the first six months of 2026.
VITAS's after-tax margin rose to 13.7% from 9.6% on the smaller Medicare Cap headwind, while Roto-Rooter's net income was essentially flat as higher marketing spend offset revenue growth.
